_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). LEFT EDGE OF THE SCROLL, second row of the summit band, and it is FULL -- no bare silk anywhere, edge to edge mountain. The subject is a system of forested ridges seen from above and across: long spurs of pale rock running diagonally down-left, each with a treed crest, separated by empty rock fans. Two things make this the most treacherous tile of the three. FIRST, the rock here is 牛毛皴 at its most extreme: the whole lower-left quadrant (x 0-0.45, y 0.55-1.0) is one enormous fan of long wandering parallel hemp-fibre strokes, sweeping down-left, and at any reduced size the fan reads as brushed hair or a spray of needles. It is stone. It is the single largest false-positive surface in the summit band and it is boxed as rock-fan-lower-left-great. SECOND, the ridge crests carry a continuous chain of 点苔 moss dots that is visually identical to the distant treelines until you look for wood -- the tell is the dotted contour line at x 0.72-0.96, y 0.42-0.58, which snakes down the open slope as a single-file chain of dots with no crowns and no trunks, and which a dab-detector will happily grab. WHERE THE REAL FOLIAGE IS: eighteen treelines and stands, all of them 遠樹/中景樹 with genuinely visible trunks. The best is the col forest at x 0.32-0.50, y 0.35-0.53 -- a stand of tall trees with clear vertical trunks and flat spreading crowns standing in the saddle between two ridges, silhouetted against pale silk, the cleanest and most animatable mass in the whole summit band. The stand immediately right of it (x 0.50-0.65) is nearly as clean, with blue-green wash behind the trunks. The bottom-right corner is different in kind: it is the top of the MID-GROUND, a habitation -- an ochre thatched-roof building with a fence line at x 0.62-0.85, y 0.92-1.0, a stand of trees with thin trunks planted behind it, and heavy near foliage clipped by the bottom edge. Those are the only near-depth objects here. ONE MORE DECOY worth naming: the dark cliff at x 0.55-0.72, y 0.55-0.82 is drawn with long VERTICAL hemp-fibre strokes hanging like a curtain -- it reads as hanging vines or a wall of needles and is bare stone. Everything continues off the right edge into t005 and off the bottom into t008.

objects.name: wooded crest along the top-left edge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. A diagonal band of merged tree crowns running down-right along the topmost crest, clipped by the top edge, with a blue-green wash smeared through it. Trunks are findable but short and thin -- the crowns have merged into one dab mass, so a tight silhouette does not exist. Perhaps 55% foliage, 45% crest rock and its own moss dotting; refine per-pixel

objects.name: treeline on the left flank, upper
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Crowns strung along the dark left-hand ridge; the ridge edge itself is moss-dotted immediately below them and the two textures touch. Keep the mask to the crowns that break the ridge silhouette

objects.name: treeline on the middle-left ridge crest
objects.note: a cleaner row than the two above: distinct crowns on visible short trunks along a crest, with pale rock behind them so the silhouette reads. Do not extend below y 0.33, where the crest turns into a bare hemp-fibre slope

objects.name: tree band along the ridge left of the col
objects.note: the west shoulder of the col forest -- taller trees than the far treelines, trunks clearly separated, crowns flat and spreading. Continuous with forest-col-centre; split only so the mask does not sweep the pale rock notch between the two ridges at about x 0.31, y 0.42

objects.name: tree stand on the left slope, lower
objects.note: an isolated group of trees with visible trunks and blue-green wash sitting on an otherwise bare pale slope -- a clean subject with an unusually generous margin of empty rock on all sides

objects.name: forest standing in the central col
objects.note: THE BEST FOLIAGE OBJECT IN THE SUMMIT BAND. A dense stand of tall trees in the saddle between two ridges: eight or more vertical trunks drawn as distinct dark strokes, flat spreading crowns above them, several outlying crowns floating clear against bare silk at the top of the box. Wood and leaf are separately visible here, so a hinge can pivot the crowns about the trunks instead of displacing the whole mass. The upper-right corner of the box is empty silk

objects.name: tree stand on the ridge right of the col
objects.note: the twin of forest-col-centre across the saddle: a rank of trunks along a ridge crest with a pale blue-green wash behind them and clear sky above. The dark flank falling away below y 0.45 is moss-dotted rock -- that is where this box must stop

objects.name: treeline on the lower central ridge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. A second, lower rank of trees below the col, crowns and trunks both legible. Sits directly above the great hemp-fibre fan, so the bottom edge of this box is the boundary between the last foliage and the biggest rock decoy in the tile -- do not let the mask bleed downward

objects.name: diagonal treeline running down the left ridge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. A line of trees marching down a crest from upper-right to lower-left; the row of trunks at about x 0.16-0.22, y 0.61-0.63 is unmistakable, but the crowns above them merge with the crest's moss dotting. Roughly the lower-left half of the box is bare fan rock

objects.name: isolated tree group low on the left slope
objects.note: a small huddle of trees with visible trunks marooned in the middle of the great hemp-fibre fan. Easy to miss and easy to over-grab: the fan strokes run straight through this box, so the mask must key on the dab crowns only. Everything around it for 0.15 in every direction is stone

objects.name: trees marching down the upper-right ridge crest
objects.note: SEARCH REGION with a low fill fraction -- perhaps 30%. Six or seven small trees strung single-file down a steep crest, each a flat crown on a short trunk, drawn with real care; but the box has to be a diagonal band's bounding rectangle, so its lower-left corner is empty pale rock. A long thin straight stroke crosses the box at about (0.75,0.10)-(0.78,0.16); it is a single bare limb or a rock seam, not foliage

objects.name: dense wooded slope in the top-right corner
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. A heavy dark mass of merged crowns filling the corner and clipped by the top edge, continuing into t001 above and t005 to the right. Trunks are mostly hidden; the mass is read as foliage on the strength of its crown silhouettes and the blue-green wash, not on visible wood. Treat the fill fraction as uncertain and mask on the dab texture

objects.name: treeline along the right-hand ridge, middle
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. A long horizontal rank of crowns along a crest with several clear trunks beneath them at x 0.73-0.80 and x 0.84-0.88. The dark mass at the right end (past x 0.90) has no legible wood and is handled separately as wooded-flank-right-edge

objects.name: dark wooded flank at the right edge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, LOWEST CONFIDENCE FOLIAGE BOX IN THIS FILE. A dark dabbed mass on a steep flank, clipped by the right edge and continuing into t005. It has the dab texture of merged crowns but no trunk survives in it. If a per-pixel pass cannot find crown structure here, demote it to rock rather than animate it -- a moving cliff is the failure this catalogue exists to prevent

objects.name: clump of leafy shrubs on the open right slope
objects.note: a sparse scatter of splayed leaf glyphs -- repeated 介-shaped and V-shaped marks with short stems, not round moss blobs -- sitting alone on an otherwise empty pale rock face, with a faint blue-green tinge. The distinction from 点苔 is the SHAPE of the mark (splayed strokes vs round dabs) and the ISOLATION (an open clump on a clear slope, not a chain following a contour). Low bushes rather than trees; box is a search region since most of its pixels are the bare rock behind

objects.name: tree stand on the bluff above the house
objects.note: tall trees with clean vertical trunks standing on the lip of a bluff, plus a second group of broad spreading crowns with blue-green wash immediately to their right. Silhouetted against pale silk above, so the top edge of the mask is clean; the bottom of the box is the dark cliff they stand on

objects.name: tree stand behind the thatched house
objects.note: the nearest legible trees in the tile: five or six slender trunks drawn as distinct thin lines with dotted crowns and a faint blue-green wash, planted behind the building's fence line. Wood and leaf clearly separated. The building's roof ridge is the hard bottom limit of this box

objects.name: near foliage at the bottom edge, left of the house
objects.note: dark, dense, large-scale leaf marks clipped by the bottom edge -- the first real mid-ground canopy, continuing into t008. Much coarser than anything else in this tile, so it will not sit in the same motion scale as the distant treelines

objects.name: great hemp-fibre rock fan, lower left quadrant
objects.note: THE PRINCIPAL DECOY OF THE SUMMIT BAND. An enormous sweep of long wandering parallel 牛毛皴 strokes fanning down-left across a fifth of the tile. At thumbnail size the fan reads as brushed fur or a spray of pine needles; a stroke-density or edge-orientation detector will score it as high as any canopy. There is not one leaf glyph, one crown, or one trunk in it. This is the family of surface that produced 'unfortunately the rock moves'. NEVER animate. The only exception inside these bounds is tree-group-left-lower-isolated

objects.name: smooth pale slope, upper centre
objects.note: a broad, almost empty rock face between the top-left crest and the right-hand ridges, drawn with faint diagonal strokes and a few contour lines. The quietest passage in the tile and a good place to verify that a mask is not over-firing: if anything here is selected as foliage, the threshold is wrong

objects.name: rock spur below the col, centre right
objects.note: the stone body of the ridge that tree-stand-ridge-right-of-col grows on, falling away below the trees. Hemp-fibre strokes plus moss dotting along its own edge -- dots on stone, not leaves

objects.name: dark cliff with hanging vertical strokes
objects.note: DECOY. A tall dark cliff face drawn with long VERTICAL hemp-fibre strokes hanging in a curtain, the darkest passage in the tile. The vertical striation mimics hanging vines or a wall of drooping needles. No crowns, no glyphs, bare stone. Rigid

objects.name: dotted contour ridge on the right slope
objects.note: DECOY, and the subtlest one here. A single-file chain of 点苔 dots snaking down an open pale slope, marking a rock contour. Isolated dark dabs on light ground is exactly the signature a foliage detector is tuned for, but a chain one dot wide that follows a contour line for 0.20 of the tile is a rock edge, not a treeline -- treelines have crowns of DEPTH and trunks under them. Rigid

objects.name: pale rock slope, lower right
objects.note: open pale slope between the shrub clump and the bottom-right habitation, sparse dotting only. Continues into t005 and t008

objects.name: thatched-roof house and fence, bottom right
objects.note: a warm-ochre hipped thatched roof with a drawn ridge line, and a horizontal fence or railing running left from it along y about 0.935. The only man-made structure in these three tiles. Clipped by the bottom edge, continues into t008. Strictly rigid -- a swaying roof destroys the read of the whole mid-ground
